intro: Video editors often ask how much do video editors make per video, but the answer depends on your ability to move from hourly billing to value based pricing. Most editors struggle because they focus on technical skills rather than the business metrics that drive client growth.
tldr: Stop charging by the hour and start pricing based on the value you provide to your client's business.
Administrative tasks consume 36% of your time; automating these is the first step to increasing your effective hourly rate.

blocks.text: Why revenue modeling is hard for video editors

The transition from creative for hire to business owner is where most editors stall. You are likely trained to think in cuts, color, and pacing, but your clients think in customer acquisition costs and retention rates. When you cannot bridge this language gap, you are trapped in an hourly model that punishes efficiency. The faster you work, the less you make.

When you bill by the hour, your income is capped by the number of hours in a day. You also invite scope creep because every revision feels like a new billable hour. This leads to burnout. You spend 36% of your time on administrative work that you cannot bill for, which effectively cuts your hourly rate by a third.
How to fix your revenue model

items: Shift to value based pricing: Price your services based on the revenue you generate for the client.
Standardize your operations: Create templates for proposals and onboarding to save time.
Use monthly retainers: Move from project based work to recurring monthly revenue to stabilize your income.
Speak the client's language: Frame your edits in terms of business impact, such as improving click through rates.

blocks.text: To start modeling your revenue, open a new file in your preferred spreadsheet app. List every project you have completed in the last six months. Calculate the total revenue and the total hours spent, including the time spent on emails and file management. This will show you your true effective hourly rate.

faq.question: How much do video editors make per video on average?
faq.answer: There is no industry standard because rates vary by complexity, client size, and your level of experience. Instead of focusing on a flat rate per video, calculate your desired annual income and divide it by your target number of projects.

faq.question: How can I stop trading time for money?
faq.answer: Package your services as a solution to a specific business problem. For example, instead of selling a video edit, sell a video strategy that increases channel retention by 20%.

faq.question: What tools do I need to track my business performance?
faq.answer: A simple spreadsheet in Google Sheets or a database in Notion is sufficient. You need to track project hours, client acquisition costs, and total revenue per month.
